summary: A 25-foot cast-iron gas beacon of 1858 in Emmet Park, Savannah, built as a range light with Fig Island; restored and relit in 2001.

structures.note: Cast-iron post 25 ft (7.6 m) tall with an ornamented shaft (LighthouseFriends); gas-lit. Taken apart into six parts in August 2000, repaired, and relit 11 January 2001.

access.note: Emmet Park on East Bay Street, Savannah. LighthouseFriends says grounds open; the USLHS place record says Open to Public: No. The sources disagree and this is not resolved.

events.note: Captain J. F. Gilmer of the Engineers proposed a harbor beacon at Savannah to the Lighthouse Board, October 1855.
Congress appropriated $2,000 on 18 August 1856 for a small light on the bay, to guide vessels from the Fig Island light.
Erected 1858 as an aid to navigation of the Savannah River; $1,969.12 was expended in 1857 and 1858 to complete it.
Lighthouse Board report, as quoted by LighthouseFriends: the beacon, being no longer a range, has been discontinued. The sources do not say when the lamp last burned.
Congress appropriated $3,000 on 3 March 1879 to move the Fig Island light and to set up a companion light on the Exchange Building.
On 1 December 1880 a light in the cupola of the Exchange Building was activated as the rear light of the Fig Island range.
March 1881: the Savannah Morning News describes the Fig Island light as in range with the light on the Exchange.
Centennial year. Trustees Garden Club develops the park area; Georgia Historical Commission marker 025-58 erected.
First week of August 2000: light disassembled into six parts; rust removed, corroded iron repaired, lenses cleaned. The Savannah Morning News and CSX Corp. each gave $62,500.
Relit in Emmet Park on 11 January 2001.

notes_for_editor: 1. Deactivation date: the record gives 1880 (deactivated). LighthouseFriends quotes the Lighthouse Board's 1869 report: the beacon, being no longer a range, 'has been discontinued'. The 1880 Exchange Building light took over the range role. The story gives both and does not settle when the lamp went out. Board annual reports for 1869-1880 are not in the local corpus (lhb covers 1891-1901 only); they should be checked. 2. Name: the record's name is Savannah Harbor Light; LighthouseFriends and the marker call it Old Harbor Light. The story uses Old Harbor Light. 3. Access: the USLHS place record shows open_to_public false; LighthouseFriends says grounds open. The story follows LighthouseFriends (a city park). Check. 4. Keepers: LighthouseFriends names the Savannah City Gas Company as keepers and says the company was paid to care for the light; the USLHS roster names two Principal Lighthouse Keepers for 1866-1869. How the two fit is not stated in the sources read. The roster lines are copied as printed and the 'person' slugs are from roster.py. Keeper names are not yet checked in a primary keeper register. 5. Wikipedia's Old Harbor Light article says the light was moved a few feet south in 1869, refurbished in 1929, turned off in World War II, and that the 1779 ships were scuttled 'to impede French and American ships'. Not cited (Wikipedia is leads only); the 1869 move and 1929 refurbishment are unverified. 6. The 1779 scuttling is stated by LighthouseFriends and by the marker; nothing else read. 7. Height and focal plane: 25 ft (7.6 m) post, 77 ft (23.5 m) focal plane (LighthouseFriends and marker agree). 8. NRHP status: the record says contributing property (Savannah Historic District); the nomination was not read, so the story does not state it. 9. SAH Archipedia's entry for the light was blocked (HTTP 403) and is not used. 10. Newspaper: a Chronicling America search for 1866-1881 Savannah beacon notices found only 1881 pages; the OCR is poor and quotes are copied from it. Earlier Savannah Morning News issues (1858-1880) were not searched further. 11. No storms, wrecks or rescues at this light appear in the sources read, so that chapter is omitted. The 1893 Savannah River lights in the corpus belong to other stations. 12. Lenses: LighthouseFriends mentions cleaned lenses in 2000; lens type not recorded.
